1.why: Four adjectives that could each describe a body, animal, or structure: grace, nimbleness, solidity, erectness are distinct qualities and none collapses into another. Nothing in the set points anywhere; 'agile' is a hunch about what a test sentence usually wants.

2.why: Four transitive verbs a legislature or official body could take as its object-verb. outlaw/enforce are opposed policy acts, review/delay are procedural; each is a serious candidate for some sentence. Pick is a hunch that 'outlaw' is the more test-like key.

3.why: Four adjectives naming distinct deficiencies (inattention, physical awkwardness, unwillingness to work, fear). No two are synonyms, so none is excluded by duplication. Pure guess.

4.why: Four concrete nouns, all of them things a plant or a growing thing can lack or compete for. Every one is legal in that frame. Guess.

5.why: Four verbs of speaking with different attitudes (grievance, firmness, proclamation, self-praise). All legal for some headword or sentence. Guess.

6.why: size and age are physical attributes, ambition and generosity are dispositions, but each can be the thing a sentence says something is judged or measured by. No exclusion available. Guess.

7.why: Four parallel participial phrases about plantings. A and D are antonyms, which is normal distractor construction, not duplication. All four legal. Guess.

8.why: Four intransitive verbs of persisting/varying/decreasing/settling. Distinct trajectories, all legal as a key for some sentence about a quantity. Guess.

9.why: Four nouns all at home in a frame about a document, book, or map (its origin, its printing, its binding, its scale). Nothing rules any out without the stem. Guess.

10.why: Four adjectives for how something came about: luck, system, improvisation, inspiration. methodical/improvised are opposed, which is a normal pairing rather than a tell. All legal. Guess.

11.why: Four adjectives of anticipatory state. patient, watchful and hopeful are all positive-to-neutral and apprehensive is negative, but a sentence could want either valence, so the asymmetry does not exclude anything. Guess.

12.why: Four verbs describing an effect on a person (deter, confuse, convince, annoy). Distinct effects, all legal. Guess.

13.why: ornate is the odd one semantically - three name a defect and it names decoration - but an ornate map, script, or frontispiece is a perfectly serious option, so it is not illegal. All four legal. Guess, and a weak one.

14.why: Four unrelated adjectives (sameness, deception, liberality, absence). Their very unrelatedness means the set constrains nothing; each needs a different sentence, and all such sentences are constructible. Guess.

15.why: Four adjectives that could describe a document, sign, or map: out of date, packed with detail, unreadable, lacking authority. All legal. Guess.

16.why: Two-blank item. brief/thorough and cautious/admiring are contrast pairs, formal/lengthy is a compatible pair, precise/silent is the weakest but a sentence contrasting precise content with a silent manner or a silent audience is constructible. Being strict, none is impossible. The pick leans on brief...thorough reading as the tidiest contrast, which is a hunch about test style, not elimination.

17.why: Four phrasal glosses about money behaviour: generous, tightfisted, prone to borrow, unable to save. All four are distinct financial characters and each could gloss a real headword. Guess.

18.why: Four adjectives for a task or a journey: dangerous, unknown, boring, difficult. No overlap tight enough to void one. All legal. Guess.

19.why: All four share the un- prefix, which is deliberate morphological parallelism rather than a leak: unyielding, unhurried, unconcerned and unreliable name four genuinely different traits, and the shared prefix gives no way to prefer one. All legal. Guess.

20.why: Four adjectives applicable to a space, a schedule, or a process. Distinct and all legal. Guess.

21.why: Four adjectives that could qualify a measure or arrangement: unlawful, incomplete, token, short-lived. partial/temporary are both partial-commitment words but along different axes (extent vs duration), so neither voids the other. All legal. Guess.

22.why: Four adjectives for a person or a manner: exhaustive, tentative, ceremonious, lenient. Unrelated to one another, all legal for some stem. Guess.

23.why: Four nouns: a settling, a written account or a best-ever mark, a departure from a rule, a beginning. record is ambiguous between two senses, which widens rather than narrows it. All legal. Guess.

24.why: All four are un- adjectives of deficiency. uncorroborated is noticeably higher register than unnecessary/unfinished/unexplained, and I am picking it on that register hunch - the harder word feeling like the key - not on elimination. Register alone is not grounds to call anything illegal, so all four stand as legal.

25.why: Inflection mismatch. totals, means and cost all fit a present-tense third-person or bare-noun slot; replaced is a past form and cannot occupy the same slot as the other three. A test would not offer it as a serious candidate alongside them, so D is illegal. That still leaves three live options and the elimination does not choose among them - cost is a guess. Flagging the set as the one genuinely incoherent option group in this batch: it is not a leak toward a single answer, it is a construction defect.
